record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.context_brief: Extension proof for cubic threefold Torelli
record.original_question: Can the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds, which reconstructs a cubic threefold from an equivalence of its Kuznetsov component with no additional assumptions on the equivalence, be proved using extension techniques for Fourier-Mukai equivalences between admissible subcategories?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to prove Theorem 6.4

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth cubic threefold. Its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves admits the semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(Y) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(Y),\, \mathcal{O}_Y,\, \mathcal{O}_Y(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(Y)$ is the right orthogonal to $\langle \mathcal{O}_Y, \mathcal{O}_Y(1)\rangle$ and is an admissible subcategory of $D^b(Y)$. The categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds asserts that for any two smooth cubic threefolds $Y, Y'$, if there exists a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence $\Phi : \mathcal{K}u(Y) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{K}u(Y')$ (with no additional hypotheses on $\Phi$), then $Y \cong Y'$.

A standard strategy in derived-categorical Torelli problems is the following extension technique: given an equivalence between admissible subcategories of two semiorthogonal decompositions, find sufficient conditions under which this equivalence can be extended to a Fourier–Mukai equivalence between the ambient bounded derived categories of the two varieties.

Problem: Can the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds, stated above with no additional assumptions on the equivalence $\Phi$, be proved purely by means of such extension techniques for Fourier–Mukai equivalences between admissible subcategories appearing in semiorthogonal decompositions?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Liu (Math. Nachr. 2024, arXiv:2304.12669) determines the group of Fourier–Mukai autoequivalences of the Kuznetsov component of a smooth complex cubic threefold and gives a new proof of the Fourier–Mukai version of the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds via extension/lifting of Fourier–Mukai functors between admissible subcategories. This addresses the question affirmatively under the assumption that the equivalence is of Fourier–Mukai type, but a proof via these extension techniques in full generality, without any assumption on the equivalence, does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: On Fourier–Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds (Liu, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the group of Fourier–Mukai autoequivalences of Ku(Y) and gives a proof of the Fourier–Mukai version of the categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: The Fourier–Mukai case of the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds is proved using methods involving admissible subcategories, giving a partial positive answer.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2304.12669 — On Fourier-Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Provides yet another proof for the Fourier–Mukai version of categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: An extension-based approach yields the categorical Torelli theorem under the Fourier–Mukai assumption on the equivalence.
